# MCPJam API

> Programmatic access to the

MCP servers in your MCPJam projects: diagnostics, tool calls, prompt rendering, and asynchronous eval runs.

> [!WARNING]
>
>
**The MCPJam API is in preview.** It works today and we use it ourselves, but\n> it has not been generally announced and the surfa
ce may change, including in\n> breaking ways, while we finish the design. Pin your integration to the\n> behaviors documented on t
his page, build a [tolerant\n> reader](#versioning--stability), and expect to revisit it. Feedback is very\n> welcome on [Discord]

(https://discord.gg/JEnDtz8X6z) or
> [GitHub](https://github.com/MCPJam/inspector/issues).

> [card] [Create an API key](https:

//app.mcpjam.com/settings/api-keys)
>
> Go straight to key management in the hosted app. If you're signed out,
> you'll be aske

d to sign in and then land right back on the API keys page.

The MCPJam API lets you operate the MCP servers saved in your
[hos

ted](https://docs.mcpjam.com/hosted/overview.md) projects (from CI, scripts, or your own agents)
without opening the UI.

What

you can do with it today:

* **Discover your resources**: list your projects, their servers, eval
 suites, and chat sessions,
so every ID the other routes need is\n self-serve\n* **Validate a server**: connect, initialize, and capture a capability snapsho
t\n* **Run the doctor**: the probe → connect → initialize → capabilities workflow\n* **Check OAuth requirements**: does this serve
r need an OAuth grant?\n* **List tools, prompts, and resources**: the server's MCP primitives\n* **Call a tool / render a prompt**
: execute primitives and get the MCP result back verbatim\n* **Read a resource** by URI\n* **Export a full snapshot**: tools, reso
urces, and prompts as one JSON document\n* **Manage a project's clients**: list, read, **create** (from a built-in\n template lik
e `claude`/`chatgpt`/`cursor`, or from a full config), edit,\n duplicate, and delete the named, reusable configurations that defi
ne how\n MCPJam connects to and talks to your MCP servers. Edits are compare-and-set:\n read the client, then send its `configId
` back as `expectedConfigId` for a\n config change and its `name` back as `expectedName` for a rename (a rename\n does not rotat
e the config, so the config token cannot detect a concurrent\n one), and a concurrent edit is rejected rather than silently rever
ted\n* **Manage a project's environments**: list, read, and archive the named\n execution bundles (host + optional server group)

that eval
 suites and goals run against,
 and **preview** what one resolves to before launching it
* **List a project's studi
es**: name, access mode, attached servers, and\n share link, and **read one study's settings**: model, system prompt,\n tool-app
roval policy, and resolved servers\n* **Author eval suites**: create a runnable suite (name, default model, servers, test cases) s
ynchronously and get a `suiteId` back; no run is started and no credits are spent\n* **Run eval suites asynchronously**: create a
run from a saved suite, get a `202` + `runId`\n immediately, then poll status, per-iteration results (tool calls, token\n usage,
latency), and full traces. Runs appear live in the hosted UI,\n tagged `source: \"api\"`\n* **Manage a server's accounts**: comp
lete OAuth yourself (e.g. the SDK's\n `runOAuthLogin`, or your CI's own sign-in) and upload the token to a named\n account; list
, rename, choose the default, and delete accounts. Tokens are\n write-only: no route returns one\n* **Run a headless agent turn**
: send a message history, get back the\n assistant reply, the platform operations it invoked, references to any\n resources it c
reated (eval suites), and token usage; the model is pinned\n server-side and billed to the project\n* **Send feedback**: report a
bug, a missing capability, or something\n confusing to the MCPJam team at the moment you hit it; the same endpoint the\n `send_

feedback` MCP tool calls

All endpoints operate on servers you have already added to a project in the
hosted inspector. Managin

g API keys remains UI-only; see
[Not in the API yet](#not-in-the-api-yet).

## Base URL

```text theme={"theme":"css-varia

bles"}
https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1
```

The API is path-versioned. All routes on this page are relative to the base
URL ab

ove.

## Authentication

Every request needs an MCPJam API key in the `Authorization` header:

```bash theme={"theme":"cs
s-variables\"}\ncurl -X POST \\\n \"https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/servers/$SERVER_ID/tools\" \\\n -H \"Auth

orization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY" \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 -d '{}'
```

### Creating a key

1. Ope
n [**Settings → API keys**](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/api-keys)\n in the hosted app (the card at the top of this page take

s you there
 directly).
2. Click **Create API key**, name it, and pick the **organization** it will act in.
3. Copy the key (

`sk_…`) immediately; **it is shown exactly once** and never
 stored by MCPJam in retrievable form.

Keys can be revoked from

the same page at any time. Revocation takes effect
immediately.

### Scope

A key is bound to one MCPJam organization at crea
tion and acts **as you,\ninside that organization**. Per-request authorization still applies: a call\nonly succeeds if the key's o

wner can access that project and server. A key
can never reach projects outside its organization.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Two delibera

te restrictions while in preview:
>
> * **API keys cannot manage API keys.** Requests to the key-management surface
> with an
`sk_…` bearer fail with `403 FORBIDDEN`. Create and revoke keys in\n> the UI.\n> * **Guest sessions cannot use the API.** Sign

in to create keys.

### Keep keys secret

Treat an API key like a password:

* Load it from an environment variable or secre
t manager; never commit it to\n source control or ship it in client-side code.\n* Scope keys narrowly: one key per integration, n
amed so you can tell them apart.\n* Rotate by creating a replacement key, switching traffic, then revoking the old one.\n* If a ke

y leaks, revoke it immediately in
 [**Settings → API keys**](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/api-keys).

If you see `401 UNAUT
HORIZED` with `details.reason: \"ORPHANED_KEY\"`, the key\nis no longer bound to an organization and cannot be used; create a new

key
from [Settings](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/api-keys).

## Conventions

**Requests.** Operations on servers are `POST
` with a JSON body (most accept\nan empty `{}`). **Reads**, the catalog listings and eval-run polling, are\n`GET` and take their o

ptions (`cursor`, `limit`, filters) as query
parameters.

**Responses.** Three envelope shapes, used consistently:

| Kind |

Shape |
| - | - |
| Single resource | The resource object directly |
| Collection | `{ "items": [...], "nextCursor": "...\
" }`; `nextCursor` omitted on the last page |\n| Error | `{ \"code\": \"...\", \"message\": \"...\", \"details\": {...} }` with a

matching HTTP status |

**Pagination.** Collections are cursor-based. Pass the previous response's
`nextCursor` as `cursor` in

the next request (body field on `POST` lists,
query parameter on `GET` lists). Cursors are opaque; don't parse them.

**Authori
ng vs running suites.** `POST /eval-suites` creates a runnable suite\n(the suite plus its test cases) **synchronously** and respon
ds `201` with the\n`suiteId`, WITHOUT running anything; author once, run later. `POST /eval-runs`\nis the async counterpart: it va
lidates and creates a run synchronously, then\ndetaches execution and responds `202` with a `runId`. Poll\n`GET /eval-runs/{runId}

` until `status` is `completed`, `failed`,
`cancelled`, or `timed_out`.
